text:
Montreal's road trip started with what the people who cover the team called its worst hockey of the season and ended with its best. The Canadiens won 3-2 in New Jersey and then 2-1 in Carolina on Thursday, trailing in the third before Lane Hutson scored both goals, the winner in overtime. They did it short-handed, and they're still short-handed tonight.

Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve with an ankle injury (ESPN estimates Nov. 25), Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks, per NHL.com, and Josh Anderson, whose contract extension is the subject of rumors, is on IR too. Zachary Bolduc has moved onto the first power-play unit and Alexandre Texier is playing almost 16 minutes a night. What holds it together is Jacob Fowler, top of The Hockey News' Calder tracker, at .924 and 14.1 goals saved above expected. Be honest about what that means: the Canadiens are +5 in goal difference on chances worth -3.9, and the goaltending is the whole gap.

The Flyers come in on a high. Down three goals in Ottawa on Thursday, they won 6-5 in overtime, and Travis Konecny, after addressing the trade rumors that have followed him (one report has the Wild as a fit while Detroit's Dylan Larkin situation stays unresolved), had his best game of the season. Rick Tocchet's team is better than its record, -21 on chances worth -11.9, but it has also only taken 43% of the five-on-five expected goals, and Dan Vladar is at .874. Trevor Zegras has two points in ten on 7.1 expected goals.

Our numbers give Montreal 3.26 expected goals to Philadelphia's 2.87, and the Canadiens a 72% playoff chance to the Flyers' 8%. Both Sleepers are Flyers: Owen Tippett at 20% to score, and Matvei Michkov, whose ice time is climbing, at 58% for a point. Juraj Slafkovsky is two points from 200 for his career but has no goals in 14 games on 5.0 expected. Cole Caufield is 40% to score.
headline: Fowler and the short-handed Habs host the comeback Flyers
